newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Blue chips push Czech PX50 higher again.
newsitem.headline: Blue chips push Czech PX50 higher again.

text.p: Czech stocks, led by major issues, continued to surge on Tuesday but analysts said it was too early to predict a sustained recovery.
The PX50 rose 2,2 percent to 520.5 while the major issue dominated RPIX gained 3.43 percent, to 1,085.5.
"The stock market was falling for quite a long term and it was time for a correction," said Pavel Sobisek of Zivnostenska Banka.
"I don't think that too many foreign investors are buying Czech stocks at the moment and if they are it's probably because of record highs in the world markets," he added.

In late February, the PX50 hit a year high of 629 but fell steadily to just over 500 during the middle of last week. The downtrend was spearheaded by the major issues which have also been at the forefront of the rebound of the last two sessions.
On Tuesday, SPT Telecom rose 140 crowns, 4.4 percent, to 3,290. CEZ was up 38 crowns, 3.9 percent, to 990 and Komercni Banka rose 85 crowns, 4.3 percent, to 2,060.
Taken together the above three shares account for 45 percent of the PX50's total capitalisation.
